'''Julia Michelle Serano''' ({{IPAc-en|s|ə|ˈ|r|æ|n|oʊ}} {{respell|sə|RAN|o}}; born 1967)<ref>Nadia Abushanab Higgins, ''Feminism: Reinventing the F-Word'', Twenty-First Century Books, 2016, p. 99.</ref> is an American writer, musician, [[spoken-word]] performer, [[transgender]] and [[bisexual]] activist, and [[biologist]]. She is known for her [[Transfeminism|transfeminist]] books, such as ''[[Whipping Girl]]'' (2007), ''Excluded'' (2013), and ''Outspoken'' (2016). She is also a public speaker who has given many talks at universities and conferences. Her writing is frequently featured in [[queer]], [[feminist]], and [[popular culture]] magazines.

==Life==
Serano has stated that she first consciously recognized in herself a desire to be [[female]] during the late 1970s, when she was 11 years old. A few years later, she began [[gender-bending]]. At first, she gender-bent secretively, but she eventually started identifying herself openly as a "male [[Cross-dressing|crossdresser]]." Serano attended her first [[support group]] for gender-bending communities in 1994 while she lived in [[Kansas]].<ref name="whippinggirl">''Serano, Julia. "Whipping Girl: A Transsexual Woman on Sexism and the Scapegoating of Femininity''," Seal Press, 2007.</ref><ref name="switchhitter"/>

Soon afterward, Serano moved to the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] where she met her wife, Dani, in 1998. During this time, Serano began identifying as not only a crossdresser but also [[transgender]] and [[bisexual]]. In 2001, she began medically [[transitioning (transgender)|transitioning]] and identifying as a [[trans woman|transgender woman]].<ref name="switchhitter">{{cite web|url=https://www.juliaserano.com/switchhitter/|title=Welcome to switch hitter dot net!|last=Serano|first=Julia|publisher=Juliaserano.com|access-date=2 November 2013}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Julia Serano at GLBT History Museum - 2.jpg|thumb|left|Julia Serano speaks at the [[GLBT Historical Society|GLBT History Museum]] in San Francisco for the launch of the second edition of ''[[Whipping Girl]]''.]]
Serano earned her PhD in [[biochemistry]] and [[molecular biophysics]] from [[Columbia University]].<ref>Her doctoral dissertation is titled: ''Messenger RNA localization in the Drosophila oocyte''</ref> She researched genetics, developmental biology, and evolutionary biology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] for 17 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://transformingcareconference.com/speaker/julia-serano/|title=Julia Serano – Transforming Care Conference|website=Transforming Care Conference|access-date=11 March 2018|archive-date=May 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190523213256/http://transformingcareconference.com/speaker/julia-serano/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/28963/title/A-Transforming-Field/|title=A Transforming Field|last=McCook|first=Alison|date=May 1, 2010|website=The Scientist|access-date=March 11, 2018}}</ref>

Serano is the author of ''[[Whipping Girl: A Transsexual Woman on Sexism and the Scapegoating of Femininity]]''. Her second book, ''Excluded: Making Feminist and Queer Movements More Inclusive'', was published on September 10, 2013, by [[Seal Press]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Excluded: Making Feminist and Queer Movements More Inclusive|last=Serano|first=Julia|date=October 2013|publisher=Basic Books |isbn = 978-1580055048}}</ref> It was named the 16th best nonfiction book of all time by readers of ''[[Ms. Magazine]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://msmagazine.com/2011/10/10/ms-readers-100-best-non-fiction-books-of-all-time-the-top-10-and-the-complete-list/ | title=Ms. Readers' 100 Best Non-Fiction Books of All Time: The Top 10 and the Complete List! - Ms. Magazine | date=October 10, 2011 }}</ref> Her third book, ''Outspoken: A Decade of Transgender Activism and Trans Feminism'', she published herself under Switch Hitter Press,<ref>{{cite book|title=Outspoken: A Decade of Transgender Activism and Trans Feminism|last=Serano|first=Julia|isbn = 978-0996881005|year = 2016|publisher=Switch Hitter Press }}</ref> which she founded along with Switch Hitter Records.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.switchhitter.net/|title=SWITCHHITTER.NET|website=switchhitter.net|access-date=26 May 2017}}</ref> ''Outspoken'' is a 2017 [[Lambda Literary Award]] finalist.<ref name="lambda-14mar2017">{{cite web|url=https://www.lambdaliterary.org/features/news/03/14/29th-annual-lambda-literary-award-finalists-announced/|title=29th Annual Lambda Literary Award Finalists Announced|date=March 14, 2017|website=Lambda Literary|access-date=March 16, 2017}}</ref> Her 2020 book, ''99 Erics: a Kat Cataclysm faux novel'', also published by Switch Hitter, won the [[Publishing Triangle]]'s 2021 Edmund White Award for Debut Fiction<ref>{{cite web |url=https://publishingtriangle.org/2021/05/winners-2021-awards/ |title=Here are the Winners of the 2021 Publishing Triangle Awards |publisher=[[Publishing Triangle]] |date= May 12, 2021|access-date=June 10, 2021 }}</ref> and was an [[Independent Publisher Book Awards|''Independent Publisher'' Book Awards]] 2021 silver medalist in LGBT+ Fiction.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://independentpublisher.com/article.php?page=2478 |title=2021 Independent Publisher Book Awards Results |work=Independent Publisher |date= |access-date=June 10, 2021 }}</ref>

Her work has appeared in [[queer]], [[feminist]], and [[pop culture]] magazines, including ''[[Bitch (magazine)|Bitch]]'', ''[[Clamor (magazine)|Clamor]]'', ''Kitchen Sink'', ''[[LiP magazine|LiP]]'', ''make/shift'', and ''[[Transgender Tapestry]]''. Excerpts of her work have appeared in ''[[The Believer (magazine)|The Believer]]'' and ''The [[San Francisco Chronicle]]'' and on [[NPR]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.litquake.org/authors/serano-julia/|title=Serano, Julia|publisher=[[Litquake]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071121123743/http://www.litquake.org/authors/serano-julia/ <!-- Bot retrieved archive -->|archive-date=November 21, 2007|access-date=21 February 2008}}</ref>

Serano has spoken about [[transgender]] and [[trans women]]'s issues at numerous universities, often at [[queer]], [[feminist]], [[psychology]], and [[philosophy]]-themed conferences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://umaine.edu/womensgenderandsexualitystudies/event/call-culture-identity-politics-political-correctness-presentation-julia-serano/|title=A Social Justice Advocate's Perspective on Call Out Culture, Identity Politics, and Political Correctness – Julia Serano|work=Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies |publisher=University of Maine|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311221432/https://umaine.edu/womensgenderandsexualitystudies/event/call-culture-identity-politics-political-correctness-presentation-julia-serano/|archive-date=March 11, 2018|access-date=March 11, 2018}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://thevitalvoice.com/trans-activist-and-writer-julia-serano-to-speak-at-webster-university/|title=Trans Activist and Writer Julia Serano to Speak at Webster University|last=Mrzljak|first=Romana|date=February 24, 2016|work=The Vital Voice|access-date=March 11, 2018|archive-date=May 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190509024551/http://thevitalvoice.com/trans-activist-and-writer-julia-serano-to-speak-at-webster-university/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://swarthmorephoenix.com/2014/02/27/queer-trans-conference/|title=Queer Trans Conference engages with safety, policing|last=Zhang|first=Henry|date=February 27, 2014|work=The Phoenix|access-date=March 11, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.citybeat.com/home/article/13006276/literary-julia-serano|title=Literary: Julia Serano|last=Gargano|first=Jason|date=November 5, 2013|work=CityBeat Cincinnati|access-date=March 11, 2018}}</ref> In 2023, she gave the keynote address at the [[Moving Trans History Forward conferences|Moving Trans History Forward conference]] at the [[University of Victoria]]. Her writings have also been used in teaching materials in [[gender studies]] courses across the United States.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Olsen |first=Sarah |date=March 19, 2015 |title=Women's History Month residency to feature trans activist and biologist |url=https://webapp2.wright.edu/web1/newsroom/2015/03/19/womens-history-month-residency-to-feature-trans-activist-and-biologist/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241126011635/https://webapp2.wright.edu/web1/newsroom/2015/03/19/womens-history-month-residency-to-feature-trans-activist-and-biologist/ |archive-date=November 26, 2024 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |work=Wright State Newsroom}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=November 11, 2014 |title=OUT100: Trans Writer Julia Serano |url=https://www.out.com/out-exclusives/out100-2014/2014/11/11/out100-trans-writer-julia-serano |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250325060817/https://www.out.com/out-exclusives/out100-2014/2014/11/11/out100-trans-writer-julia-serano |archive-date=March 25, 2025 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |work=OUT Magazine}}</ref>

Serano is a [[poetry slam|slam poet]] and has given spoken-word performances at universities as well as at events such as the [[National Queer Arts Festival]], San Francisco [[gay pride|Pride]] [[Dyke March]] and [[Trans March]] stages, [[Ladyfest]], outCRY!, Femme 2006 and in ''[[The Vagina Monologues]]''.<ref name="seranobio">{{cite web |title=Julia Serano Renaissance Woman! |url=https://www.juliaserano.com/about.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250618201821/https://www.juliaserano.com/about.html |archive-date=18 June 2025 |access-date=20 February 2008 |website=juliaserano.com}}</ref> She was a guitarist and vocalist for the band Bitesize from 1997 through the early 2000s and has also recorded solo music.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Serano |first=Julia |title=Bitesize! -hammering the final nail into indie rock's coffin- |url=http://www.bitesize.net/about.html |publisher=Bitesize! |access-date=26 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120420155947/http://www.bitesize.net/about.html |archive-date=April 20, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Serano organizes and hosts ''GenderEnders'', a performance series that features the work of transgender, [[intersex]], and [[genderqueer]] artists and allies that has produced 20 shows. She received a grant to curate "The Penis Issue: Trans and Intersex Women Speak Their Minds," a spoken-word event, as part of the 2007 [[National Queer Arts Festival]].<ref name="seranobio" />

She writes social justice articles on the website ''[[Medium (website)|Medium]]'' about topics like transgender identity, LGBTQ+ visibility, and identity politics.<ref name="js-medium">{{cite web |title=Julia Serano - Medium |url=https://medium.com/@juliaserano |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250610080318/https://juliaserano.medium.com/ |archive-date=June 10, 2025 |access-date=January 24, 2020 |publisher=[[Medium (website)|Medium]]}}</ref><ref name="Vox">{{Cite web |last=Lopez |first=German |date=August 9, 2016 |title=The debate about transgender children and "detransitioning" is really about transphobia |url=https://www.vox.com/2016/8/9/12404246/transgender-children-detransitioning-transphobia |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427041715/https://www.vox.com/2016/8/9/12404246/transgender-children-detransitioning-transphobia |archive-date=April 27, 2025 |access-date=June 30, 2025 |website=Vox |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Serano lives in [[Oakland, California]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://diversity.lbl.gov/2020/06/16/pride-month-a-conversation-with-julia-serano/ | title=Pride Month: A Conversation with Julia Serano – June 24, 2020 | access-date=October 24, 2022 | archive-date=March 28, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328030343/https://diversity.lbl.gov/2020/06/16/pride-month-a-conversation-with-julia-serano/ | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Carstensen |first1=Jeanne |date=June 22, 2017 |title=Julia Serano, Transfeminist Thinker, Talks Trans-Misogyny |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/22/us/lgbt-julia-serano-transfeminist-trans-misogyny.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250228134351/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/22/us/lgbt-julia-serano-transfeminist-trans-misogyny.html |archive-date=February 28, 2025 |access-date=June 30, 2025 |newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref>
